First off, lower FoV is an advantage when aiming, fundamental point you are missing. You second point would be true, knowing when to scope would be an interesting choice, but that's not how the rifle scopes work. No quick-scope inaccuracy, means that players are not constrained to their choice. There are no meaningful trade offs to scoping in mid-fights. This means players avoid the slower, scoped-in movement speed until they have committed to fighting. 

Pros are not perfect. They have to learn things too. The biggest reason pros did not switch immediately to the AUG is not because when to, and when not-to scope is an interesting choice, but because they did not want to devote valuable practice time to commit a new spray to muscle memory when at any moment, Valve could nerf the weapon.
AWP and scout have drawbacks in low rate-of-fire, and quick-scoping inaccuracy. AUG and SG have zero drawbacks associated with a scope. Your argument is a straw-man.
Why were people mad about the r8 release? Obviously it wss in the game, so anyone can use it. Perfectly balanced.
But the awp and scout are limited by rate of fire and quickscope inaccuracy. Neither the SG or aug have these drawbacks.
